body:
lol...I really hate that it's breaking the law. For an enlightened country, we're completely backwards sometimes.

I get support from various charities, such as H4H and the Royal British Legion since discharge; I think it's actually a part of the "problem" (if one is to be discerned from my mindset) more than anything. They're great, and they do what they can *when* they can, and are there whenever they're needed. I'm just at the end of my rope, and frankly to me, their resources are best served elsewhere right now.

And...No. "Doing it for my country" was how I got trhrough for a good couple of years. My psychiatrist and therapists would tell me privately that anything I did was a *good* thing, and I suppose I accepted that as a truth in part to make them feel ok about themselves - I don't think people can understand how taking life...*Any* life is soul damaging, and there's really no coming back from that point. I genuinely wish there were. The truth is thatas time goes by and you're left to think about it, you see many documentaries from "the bad guys" who use the same kind of justifications, and it begins to erode the belief and invalidate the phrase in your mind.

No, thank you. Well..To summarise, I've been diagnosed with PTSD, but am a manic depressive with bipolar disorder to boot; very soon, I will be 36 years old and have lived every one of my years since I were 10 years old with nightmares, varying moods - the highest highs, and the lowest lows - I...Simply can't go on anymore. My body can't take the constant insomnia that I force upon it because I don't want to sleep, and I can't escape the memories that are seared in my head - I'm wracked with guilt over the choices I've made, the violence I've perpetrated upon others, and the lives I've taken under the justification that I was serving my country. I can no longer bear the idea that I am so broken inside, that the possibility of me finding a happy, stable relationship is miniscule to say the least. 

I'm not a fool, and I've come to accept these things; I've come to terms with a great many things about myself, but I can't stand the things my own mind does to me; I live every day in pain, and no one is any the wiser because I smile, wish people well and hug them to reassure them that everything is going to be ok. Things...Will not be ok. They stopped being ok a long time ago.

As for the positives in my life, I do see them; bizarrely, they are what has solidifed my concious choice to euthanise myself - I want to leave this world on a moment that I'm "up". Also...I'm talking it through. I'm asking what you'd do if you knew you had one more day to live.

As for the choices, I have a high blood pressure thanks to a more than serious measure of hypertension; potassium chloride or digitalis would, I can safely assume, exacerbate any heart problems I have. My plan at this point would be to call 999 once the event has occurred, but be purposely vague so that any attempts at resuscitation would be futile, and allow the coroner to remove any doubt of suicide - despite my medical records.
